newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London ended firmer on active short covering on the strength of New York arabica futures. By the close, the March contract was $32 higher at $1,264 per tonne while front-month January gained $28 to close at $1,331 per tonne.

In New York the soon-too-expire December contract exploded to the upside which dragged the other months higher as well, although with more limited gains. December added 4.65 cents/lb to close at 117.75 cents/lb while March closed 2.60 cents/lb higher at 108.20 cents/lb. The outer months added 0.90 to 2.50 cents/lb higher.

The upturn is regarded as a technical correction to last week's slide to seven-week lows. Moreover, prompt physical supplies remain tight. Another factor was the uncertainty about the size of the 1997/98 Brazilian crop which will keep market participants focused on supplies.

Recent forecasts for the Brazilian 1997/98 crop have ranged widely between 17.8 and 32 million 60-kg bags versus around 26-27 million bags in 1996/97. Traders said that March and the deferred positions will likely take on a more defensive posture once December expires next week.

INDONESIA - According to the Association of Indonesian Coffee Exporters (AEKI) coffee production in coffee year 1996/97 (October/September) is likely to remain at last year's level of 7.5 million 60-kg bags. Also exports are expected to remain at the 1995/96 level of 5.6 million bags. The production figures for coffee year 1996/97 differ significantly from the crop year figures. According to industry sources coffee production in crop year 1996/97 (April/March) could total 7.5 million bags up from 6.4 million bags the previous year.

BRAZIL - Exports of Brazilian instant coffee totalled 58,000 tonnes in 1996 against 60,365 tonnes in 1995, a drop of 3.9 per cent, the Brazilian Soluble Coffee Industry Association (ABICS) said. However, revenue was 9.98 per cent lower at $430 million against $477.7 million in 1995. Russia was the largest importer of Brazilian soluble coffee, buying 26,362 tonnes in the last 12 months which represented 45.4 per cent of total sales. Total exports in 1997 are expected to drop 0.86 per cent to 57,500 tonnes and total revenue to fall 10.77 per cent to $383.7 million next year.

ABICS has contracted international lawyers to prepare a legal challenge to the European Union preferential tariff system. The EU tariff on Brazilian soluble coffee will rise to 10.1 per cent in 1997 up from a 1996 rate of 9.0 per cent. No import tariff is charged on soluble coffee from other producing countries in Latin America and Africa as the EU considers Brazil to be more developed than other nations. The Brazilians fear that the uneven tariff structure is allowing other countries to replace Brazilian soluble exports.

UNITED STATES - The United States imported 1.482 million bags of coffee in September 1996, nearly 16 per cent more than was imported the same month in 1995. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1996 up to 14.472 million bags, nearly 17 per cent more than was imported the same period 1995. Total imports in calendar year 1995 rose by 5.8 per cent to 17.105 million bags.

Major suppliers of green coffee in January/September 1996 were Guatemala (1.228 vs 1.222 million bags), Mexico (3.151 vs 2.283 million bags), Brazil (1.077 vs 1.864 million bags) and Colombia (2.136 vs 1.655 million bags).

The country exported 1.488 million bags of coffee in Januray/September 1996, 15 per cent more than was exported the same period in 1995. Total exports in calendar year 1995 fell by 22 per cent to 1.841 million bags.
